subject: [PATCH bpf-next v3 0/4] bpf: Check recursion per task for preemptible programs

reviews.author: Alexei Starovoitov
reviews.summary: Reviewer Alexei Starovoitov suggested that if the design of private stacks is being revised, it should be based on the existing insert_arena_stack_get() function, which has lower overhead and no artificial limits.
reviews.raw_body:
If you want to redesign private stack please take inspiration
from insert_arena_stack_get(). Much lower overhead and no artificial limits.

reviews.author: JP (CrowdStrike) (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that their concurrency-safe private stacks concept is not necessary for the current patch series and will be pursued separately.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for taking a look. Since it looks like v4 will conditionally disable
preemption for run context entry to exit, this concept does not have to be
tied to this series.

We'll pursue the private stack work separately, but will continue testing
revisions of this series.

2026-11-25.patch_summary: This patch proposes a new approach to concurrency-safe private stacks in Linux, which are currently used by BPF programs. The existing per-prog per-cpu model is not sufficient for concurrent tasks on the same CPU, leading to potential corruption and overflow/underflow issues. The proposed solution introduces a per-prog per-cpu pool of private stacks, where each program acquires an available slot at invocation time and releases it on exit. This allows multiple tasks to use separate private stacks concurrently, eliminating the need for marking private stacks and enabling the use of a new per-task per-prog recursion guard. The patch is a proof-of-concept implementation for x86_64 trampolines and has been validated with bpftrace programs.
